title: The Lucena Position
subtitle: Build a bridge — the most famous winning technique.
goals: Build the bridge with the rook lift

steps.say: The Lucena position — printed in chess books since 1497 and still the single most important rook endgame. Your pawn stands on the seventh with your king in front of it; the enemy king is cut off by your rook; the enemy rook waits to check you forever. Every rook ending you ever win 'up a pawn' funnels toward this exact picture — so the winning method is mandatory knowledge.

steps.prompt: Your king can't step out — endless checks await. Prepare his escape route: play the famous rook lift!
hints: If the king emerges now, the enemy rook checks him back to e8 forever. He needs a shelter waiting for him.
Rf4! The rook will later swing to e4, blocking the checks — chess calls it 'building a bridge'.

line.say: THE BRIDGE! The rook takes the fourth rank — soon the king will walk out, absorb a few checks, and duck behind this rook like a wall. Remember this lift: it wins every Lucena.

rejections.say: Rd2+! Ke6, Re2+! Kd6, Rd2+... the checks never end, because the king has no shelter — he must crawl back to e8. Build the bridge FIRST: Rf4.
One rank too far! The king's walk will need e5 for himself. The classic bridge goes to the FOURTH rank — Rf4 — so Re4 blocks the checks at exactly the right moment.

steps.wrongSay: The king needs cover before he steps out. The rook lift to the fourth rank prepares it.
steps.successSay: Rf4 — four hundred years of endgame theory in one rook move.

steps.prompt: Bridge ready (Black marked time with Ra1). Now walk the king out and PROVE the technique — the full sequence to the end!
hints: Step the king out toward the rook's rank: he'll zigzag d7, e6, d6, e5, taking the checks as they come.
When the final check flies, the rook drops to e4 — the bridge closes and the checks are over forever.

line.say: Out into the storm — the checks begin!
Zigzagging down, always toward the bridge...
The king weaves — each check pushes him closer to shelter.
One step from the wall — the rook has one check left...
THE BRIDGE CLOSES! The rook blocks the final check, the king shelters behind it, and e8=Q cannot be prevented. That is the Lucena — the position every rook endgame dreams of becoming.

rejections.say: A spite check — after Kg6 attacks your rook you've achieved nothing and the pawn still can't promote. The plan is the king walk: Kd7, ride the checks, and close the bridge on e4.

steps.wrongSay: March the king out — d7 first — and zigzag toward the waiting rook. The bridge does the rest.
steps.successSay: You just played a sequence studied continuously for five centuries. This IS rook endgame technique.

steps.prompt: Desperate, Black threw his rook onto the bridge. Finish cleanly!
hints: The rook capture is free — and then nothing on the board stops the pawn.
Take, and promote. Count Black's king: two moves too slow.

line.say: ...and the pawn crowns just as the black king arrives one move late. Lucena complete: bridge, walk, block, QUEEN.

rejections.say: Retreating leaves the rook alive to harass you all over again. It hangs with no defender in sight — take it, and the pawn queens unopposed.

steps.wrongSay: A whole rook is en prise with check resolved — take it, then promote.
steps.successSay: From cut-off king to new queen: you now own the most important winning method in rook endgames.
